Title-memory buffers on an ID3D12Device3::OpenExistingHeapFromAddress heap (CPU and GPU share bytes, Map returns the title VA) are implemented and tested but opt-in (TOMBOX_ALIAS_TITLE=1): the PC runtime pins the allocation, so VirtualFree/UnmapViewOfFile fail while the heap is open (test title_heap_does_not_block_unmap_or_free), and mapped xmem views are never used. Tests alias::two_placements_at_one_va_share_title_memory, two_textures_at_one_va_share_gpu_local_heap, local_span_covers_the_reservation. Buffers placed at VAs finer than 64 KB (Fortnite sub-allocates at 8 KB) now share their page (dev-b, placed_offset.rs): each one is its own placed buffer at the 64 KB base on the same alias heap, widened by its page offset, with a per-resource GPU-VA offset. That offset is applied in GetGPUVirtualAddress, gpu_va lookups, Map/console map_x copies, device SRV/UAV FirstElement and counter offset, and the CL CopyBufferRegion/CopyTextureRegion footprint/CopyResource/CopyResourceX/ResolveQueryData/SetPredication/ExecuteIndirect offsets. It is dropped when the resource dies. Test placed_offset::sub_page_buffers_share_the_page_with_their_own_gpu_va_offset runs on a real device: GPU VAs differ by the page offset, a copy into the sub-page buffer leaves both neighbours intact, and CopyResource copies only its own bytes. A title VA fill (fill.rs via gpu_va::lookup) lands at the right page byte. That check also exposed a wrong ID3D12Resource IID in fill.rs, which made every GPU pattern fill fail with E_NOINTERFACE; it is now fixed. Residuals closed (dev-b): GetDesc reports the title's width (resource vtable slot 10). CL 83 CopyTextureRegionX shifts placed-footprint offsets, using 0x30-byte copy locations with RowPitch kept. The CopyResource/CopyResourceX buffer shortcut notes GPU writes. An own release watch drops the offset, and on attach failure the placement falls back to committed. DiscardResource on a buffer does no GPU work, as in console xgs12 0x38020, which only discards kinds 3/4. Uneven typed/structured views use a helper placed buffer 64 KB steps lower on the same heap so the first element is exact. MSAA: alias heaps of 4 MB or more are 4 MB-aligned, so MSAA placements at 4 MB heap offsets share the alias heap (msaa_place.rs). Message ring: unread messages stay until popped and new ones are not written while the ring is full (console valid-slot ring), so a title that never pops (Fortnite waits on fences) keeps the oldest 0x1000. Command types no analysed title issues return E_NOTIMPL.
notes.SHAPE: XMA (Fortnite CPU-read streaming, 0x1406de4ec/0x1406de56c/0x1406f296c/0x1406f2ef0), SRC + DMA flowgraphs (XDefiant Wwise), DMA reader rings (Terraria FMOD 0x1410264d0) run on host threads; independent XMA voices decode in parallel across host cores (one voice per thread, so each voice completes in console order). Verified by crates/tests/audio_titles (20 tests, incl. SRC ratio 1.5 pitch-up; parallel voices run on a persistent tombox-shape-xma worker pool, not per-call threads: 4 XDefiant voices (stereo, mono, 44.1 kHz and 32 kHz SRC) enabled by one mask and mixed in one flowgraph, each exact, real XDefiant XMA through Fortnite's exact call sequence with output == SamplesEncoded, 6 voices on 6 threads bit-exact, SRC ratios 0.91875/0.66667 stretch duration exactly, FMOD init/disconnect/reinit, ApuHeapGetState/ApuFree accounting, ApuMapApuAddress/ApuMapVirtualAddress round trip) and crates/compat/acphal unit tests.

notes.XAudio2Create: Fortnite passes XAUDIO2_DO_NOT_USE_SHAPE (0x400) at all three XAudio2Create call sites (processors 8, 8, 0); its mixer submits float PCM source voices (pBufferWMA NULL), the legacy path PCM/xWMA only, and XMA is decoded through FXMAAudioInfo on AcpHal SHAPE, so Fortnite never creates an XMA2 XAudio2 voice and audible Fortnite audio depends on the AcpHal SHAPE path. With 0x400 the console engine is the shared XAudio2 codebase, so crates/compat/xaudio2_9 returns the System32 host engine unwrapped (processor 0 -> console default 0x20, CoIncrementMTAUsage for the console's implicit MTA); without 0x400 it wraps the engine and decodes XMA2 source voices in software via the xma crate with console sample numbering (GCXAudioExt 0xa380/0xa610: sample S = frame S/512, subframe (S%512)/128; no first-frame or 64-sample drop).
